title: Rapid UI Standardization for Boutique E-commerce
business: A boutique e-commerce agency managing dozens of unique storefronts for independent retailers.
problem: The agency struggles with CSS bloat and inconsistent design tokens across projects, leading to high maintenance costs when updating global brand styles.
solution: Tailwind CSS provides a utility-first approach that enforces design consistency through a shared configuration, allowing developers to build interfaces by composing small, reusable classes directly in markup.
steps: Initialize a Vite project for the new storefront.
Install tailwindcss and the @tailwindcss/vite plugin via npm.
Register the plugin in the vite.config.ts file to enable the build-time engine.
Add the @import 'tailwindcss' directive to the primary CSS entry point.
Apply utility classes directly to HTML elements to construct the UI without writing custom CSS files.
outcome: Developers achieve a unified visual language across all client sites while eliminating the need to manage large, cascading stylesheets that often conflict with one another.
limitation: The utility-first approach can lead to verbose HTML markup, making templates harder to read; developers should check for excessive class repetition and consider component extraction when patterns become too complex.
